newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing debt market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing debt market report.

text.p: Dutch bonds lost most of their early morning gains during Monday afternoon, as traders deemed gains inspired by bullish U.S. overdone, dealers said.
"We slid away today. There's been quite a growth in prices which the market needs some time to digest," a trader said.
Bonds were little higher than on Friday by the close, although traders said some short coverage on longer dated issues, notably the Jan 2023 bond, resulted in moderate curve flattening.
The market still suffered from poor investor interest. Most trades were instead between market professionals.
"We're waiting for a retracement and we'll see if end-investors decide to test these levels," one dealer said.
However, traders said there appeared little scope for immediate investor excitement with prevailing low yields, particularly at the longer end.
"The ten year (yield) closed at 6.06 (percent). People will tend to sell rather than buy at those levels," one trader said.
